# `read_file` silently reads to EOF when `line_end < line_start`

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a] and deliberately left out of that fix's
scope to keep its review surface to one function.

`read_file` (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`) computes
`hi = line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else len(lines)`. An INVERTED range — `line_end`
below `line_start` — therefore falls back to "read to EOF" (capped at `_READ_MAX_LINES`) rather
than reporting that the request was malformed. The agent asked for a 30-line window and silently
received a 259-line one.

Observed live: the looping verifier in bf31 issued
`read_file(<path>, line_start=115, line_end=30)` **31 times**, each returning the same 11,000-char
blob. The malformed range was not the cause of that loop, but it is the same class of defect as the
one bf31 fixed — a tool answering a request it did not actually perform, with no signal that it
substituted something else.

Note the deliberate, documented case that must be preserved: `line_end=0` means "read to EOF" and is
part of the tool's contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `read_file` with `line_end < line_start` (and `line_end != 0`) returns an explicit `Error: ...`
      naming the malformed range, instead of silently reading to EOF
- [x] `line_end == 0` still means "read to EOF, capped" — the documented behaviour is unchanged
      (regression pinned)
- [x] a normal `line_start <= line_end` window is unchanged
- [x] the docstring states the malformed-range behaviour, since Pydantic AI passes it to the agent
      as the tool contract (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:46`)
